skills.name: start
skills.title: Founder Intake and Company Profile
skills.purpose: Create the single source of truth every other skill reads: the company profile. Legal, tax, accounting, privacy, employment, and outreach rules all depend on where the company and its customers are, so collect that first and never assume it.
inputs: Where the HQ will be, and whether the company is incorporated
Founder citizenship and tax residence
Countries of first customers and of any workers
Product, stage, funding plan, budget, tools
workflow: Answer the location and legal questions, starting with where the HQ will be.
Describe the company: product, type, unit of work, stage, funding plan.
Set operating constraints: launch date, weekly hours, budget, tools, languages, approval preference.
Review the generated company profile and confirm it.
Derive the jurisdiction set and the professional reviews needed (lawyer, accountant, tax adviser) per country.
Pick the next skill from the route recommended for your stage.
deliverables: Jurisdiction set and list of professional reviews needed
gates: The completed profile before any other skill relies on it
Any later change to HQ country, legal form, or approval rules

skills.name: launch-sprint
skills.title: Launch Sprint: Idea to Operating Company in 14 Days
skills.purpose: Orchestrate every skill into one 14-day plan with daily goals and exit gates. The sprint produces a company that is formed or in formation, a product in the hands of pilot customers, a working revenue funnel, and operating routines for finance, operations, and support.
inputs: Company profile
Weekly hours and budget
Work already done
workflow: Set expectations: registration, banking, tax IDs, and trademarks run on third-party clocks; start them on day 1.
Tailor the reference plan to stage, HQ country, weekly hours, and budget; remove work already done.
Identify long-lead items for the jurisdiction and schedule them first.
Write the sprint plan: for each day the goal, skills, deliverables, founder decisions, and exit gate.
Each day, open with the day brief, run the skills, and close with a status update.
Enforce the gates. If a gate fails, stop and choose: narrow scope, change segment, or extend.
Keep one risk list across functions and review it at each gate.
On day 14, run the launch readiness review and hand over to the weekly review.
gates: The tailored plan and any extension of the calendar
Each gate decision (G1 to G5)
Every external, financial, or irreversible action raised during the sprint

skills.name: founder-weekly-review
skills.title: Founder Weekly Operating Review
skills.purpose: Give the founder one page each week covering every function, the decisions only the founder can make, and the three priorities that matter, so the company runs on a cadence without meetings.
inputs: Outputs of the area skills: cash and runway, pipeline, product metrics, operations, support, compliance calendar
Last week's priorities and decision log
workflow: Collect the numbers from each area: cash and runway, revenue and pipeline, activation and retention, AI quality and cost per task, uptime and incidents, support volume and satisfaction, deadlines in the next 30 days.
Compare with last week and with plan; mark each area green, amber, or red with one sentence of cause.
Review last week's priorities: done, moved, dropped, and why.
List decisions waiting on the founder with a recommendation for each.
List approvals queued by other skills (payments, filings, sends, deployments).
Propose the week's three priorities, chosen by effect on the current company milestone, and what will be deliberately ignored.
Schedule the work: which skills run when, and which are delegated to scheduled tasks.
Write the summary and update the decision log.
gates: The three priorities
Each queued approval, individually
handoffs: Any area skill for the work chosen

skills.name: stack-and-automation-setup
skills.title: Tool Stack and Automation Setup
skills.purpose: Select the smallest tool stack that covers every function, connect it to Claude, and schedule the recurring work so the company operates between founder sessions.
inputs: Company profile, budget, tools already in use
Connectors available in the founder's Claude environment
workflow: List the tool categories in `CONNECTORS.md` and record what the founder already uses for each.
Recommend one tool per uncovered category, preferring tools with a Claude connector or an API, a free or low entry tier, and availability in the HQ country.
Check which connectors are installed and working; guide connection of the missing ones; note categories that will run on file export and manual steps.
Write the chosen stack to the company profile.

Define the automation schedule: daily (lead response, support triage, outbound replies), weekly (bookkeeping, pipeline review, CRM hygiene, founder review, content), monthly (close, investor update, compliance sweep, cost review), quarterly (health checks, pricing and policy reviews).
For each scheduled run, define the trigger, the skill, the inputs, what it may do unattended, and what it must queue for approval.
Create the scheduled tasks where the environment supports it; otherwise produce a calendar of manual triggers.
Review automation monthly: runs completed, approvals pending, failures, time saved.
gates: Any paid tool subscription
Granting a connector access to email, bank, or production systems
What each scheduled run may do without approval
handoffs: Every area skill uses the stack recorded in the profile

skills.name: legal-entity-formation
skills.title: Entity Formation
skills.purpose: Choose the right jurisdiction and legal form for an Applied AI or Agentic AI company and take the founder from decision to a registered, bankable entity. Always ask where the HQ will be before recommending anything; the answer drives every downstream legal and finance skill.
inputs: HQ country (and state or province), founder citizenship and tax residence
Fundraising intent (bootstrapped, angels, venture) and expected investor geography
Target customer geography and whether enterprise buyers require a local entity
Planned hiring countries in the next 12 months
workflow: Confirm the HQ location and founder tax residence. If either is missing from the profile, ask and write the answer to the profile.
Shortlist two or three structures (for example local entity only, foreign holding plus local subsidiary, or a common venture vehicle) using `references/jurisdiction-playbook.md` as the starting map.
Research current formation rules for each shortlisted option: minimum capital, director and residency requirements, registered-office and agent needs, timeline, cost, and ongoing obligations.
Compare the options in a decision table: investor familiarity, founder tax exposure, administrative load, time to bank account, and cost to unwind.
Recommend one option and state what would change the recommendation.

Draft the formation pack as document text ready for a lawyer to mark up, not as a list of items: name-availability check, constitutional documents (articles, bylaws, or deed), initial director and officer appointments, share issuance to the founder, registered office, and beneficial-ownership filings.
Produce the post-formation checklist: tax ID, bank account, statutory registers, founder share payment, IP assignment, and the first board resolutions.
Give a realistic timeline. Flag when registration or banking will take longer than the 14-day sprint and list what can proceed in parallel.
deliverables: Draft formation documents and filing checklist for the chosen jurisdiction
Post-formation checklist with owners and dates
Questions for the local lawyer and for the tax adviser
gates: Choice of jurisdiction and legal form
Submission of any registry filing and payment of any fee
Share numbers, par value, and capital contributed
handoffs: `legal-founder-equity-and-cap-table` for vesting, IP assignment, and the cap table
`finance-setup` for bank account, tax registrations, and chart of accounts

skills.name: legal-founder-equity-and-cap-table
skills.title: Founder Equity, IP Assignment, and Cap Table
skills.purpose: Keep ownership clean from day one: founder shares, vesting, intellectual-property assignment, option pool, advisor grants, and a cap table that reconciles to the statutory share register.
inputs: Entity documents and share capital from formation
Everyone who has contributed code, design, data, or prompts so far, and under what terms
Planned advisors, early hires, and pool size
workflow: Build the cap table: holders, share class, number, price paid, date, vesting terms, and fully diluted percentages. Reconcile it to the share register.
Draft the founder share subscription or purchase agreement with a vesting or reverse-vesting mechanism valid in the jurisdiction.
Identify tax elections or filings with hard deadlines tied to the grant date (for example an election on restricted stock) and put them at the top of the task list.
Draft the IP assignment covering all pre-incorporation work, including code, models, prompts, datasets, domains, and brand assets. List any third-party or prior-employer IP risk.
Design the equity incentive pool: size, instrument suited to the jurisdiction, approval steps, and valuation requirement.
Draft advisor and early-contributor agreements with vesting and IP clauses.
Model dilution for the next round and present pre- and post-money tables.
Set the update procedure: every issuance, transfer, or grant updates the cap table, the register, and the board approval record in the same session.
deliverables: Cap table (spreadsheet or ~~cap table tool) with fully diluted view
Founder share agreement and vesting schedule draft
IP assignment agreement draft and IP inventory
Option or incentive plan summary and approval checklist
gates: Vesting terms and any acceleration
Pool size and each individual grant
Signing of the IP assignment
handoffs: `legal-corporate-governance` for the board and shareholder approvals each issuance needs

skills.name: legal-fundraising
skills.title: Fundraising Legal Workflow
skills.purpose: Run the legal side of a raise end to end: pick the instrument, prepare the documents and data room, review investor terms, obtain approvals, and close with the cap table updated.
inputs: Target amount, valuation expectations, investor list and their countries
Current cap table and constitutional documents
Any existing convertible instruments or side letters
workflow: Select the instrument suited to the jurisdiction and stage: SAFE or local equivalent, convertible note, or priced equity round. Explain the trade-offs in plain language.
Check securities-law constraints on who may be offered shares and what filings follow a closing in the company's and each investor's jurisdiction.
Model the round: cap, discount, pool top-up, pro-rata rights, and resulting ownership under three price scenarios.

Assemble the data room: corporate records, cap table, IP assignments, key contracts, financials, product and security documentation, and AI-specific items (model providers, data sources, evaluation results).

Review any term sheet clause by clause: economics, control, protective provisions, liquidation preference, anti-dilution, founder vesting resets, information rights. Rate each clause standard, negotiable, or unusual.
Draft the closing set: investment agreement or instrument, board and shareholder approvals, updated constitutional documents if required, and disclosure schedule.
Run the closing checklist: signatures, funds received, shares or instruments issued, registers and cap table updated, regulatory filings made.
Prepare the investor-update template for after closing.
deliverables: Term-sheet review memo with negotiation positions
gates: Instrument, valuation cap, and total amount
Any term rated unusual
Signature of every investor document
handoffs: `finance-fundraising-and-investor-relations` for the deck, investor pipeline, and updates
`finance-planning-and-runway` for the financial model investors will ask for

skills.name: legal-corporate-governance
skills.title: Board, Shareholders, Minutes, and Resolutions
skills.purpose: Run corporate governance for a company with one founder and a growing set of shareholders and directors: decide which body must approve what, prepare meetings or written consents, record minutes, and keep the statutory books current.
inputs: Constitutional documents and any shareholders' agreement
Current directors, officers, and shareholders
The action that needs approval, or the meeting date
workflow: Classify the action: director decision, shareholder decision, or both, using the constitutional documents and local company law. State the required majority, notice period, and quorum.
Choose the route allowed locally: meeting, written resolution, or unanimous consent. Note where a notary or registry filing is required.
Draft the notice, agenda, and board pack (CEO report, financials, key metrics, decisions requested).
Draft the resolutions in the local form, with recitals, the operative decision, and authority to execute.
After the meeting or consent, write minutes: attendees, quorum, conflicts declared, discussion summary, decisions, votes, and action items.
Update the statutory registers (directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, charges) and file any registry notifications within the deadline.
Store signed records in the corporate minute book with an index.
Maintain a standing calendar: board cadence, annual general meeting, accounts approval, and annual return.
deliverables: Resolutions or written consents ready to sign
gates: Content of every resolution before circulation
Sending notices to directors or shareholders
Any registry filing
handoffs: `finance-planning-and-runway` for the financial section of the board pack

skills.name: legal-commercial-contracts
skills.title: Commercial Contracts
skills.purpose: Build and operate the contract stack an AI company sells and buys on: templates, review of counterparty paper, negotiation positions, signature, and a contract register.
inputs: Product description, pricing model, and delivery model (SaaS, API, agent acting on customer systems)
Customer type (consumer, SMB, enterprise, public sector) and countries
Model and infrastructure providers and their terms
workflow: Define the contract stack for the business model: terms of service or master agreement, order form, data processing agreement, service levels, acceptable use policy, NDA, and partner or reseller terms.

Draft each template under the governing law chosen in the profile, with AI-specific clauses: customer data and training use, output ownership, accuracy disclaimers, human-oversight responsibilities, agent action authority and limits, and sub-processors.
Align the templates with upstream provider terms so the company never promises what its model or cloud provider does not allow.
Write a negotiation playbook: preferred position, fallback, and walk-away for liability cap, indemnity, IP, data, termination, and payment.
For counterparty paper, review clause by clause against the playbook and return a redline with a short issues list ranked by risk.
Route for signature through ~~e-signature and store the executed copy.
Maintain the contract register: parties, value, term, renewal and notice dates, unusual obligations.
deliverables: Redlines and issues lists for reviewed contracts
gates: Any deviation beyond the playbook fallback
Uncapped liability, exclusivity, or IP transfer
Sending for signature
handoffs: `legal-privacy-and-ai-compliance` for the DPA and transfer mechanisms

skills.name: legal-privacy-and-ai-compliance
skills.title: Privacy, Data Protection, and AI Regulation
skills.purpose: Establish the privacy and AI-regulatory baseline for a product that processes customer data through models and autonomous agents, and keep the evidence a customer or regulator will ask for.
inputs: Data categories processed, sources, and data subjects' locations
Model providers, hosting regions, sub-processors
What the product or agent decides or does without a human
workflow: Determine which regimes apply from where the company, customers, and data subjects are: general privacy law, sector rules, and AI-specific regulation.
Map data flows: collection, prompts, retrieval stores, model calls, logs, analytics, and retention. Record legal basis and purpose for each.
Classify the AI use case under the applicable AI regulation and list the resulting obligations (transparency, human oversight, documentation, prohibited uses).
Draft the public documents: privacy notice, cookie notice, AI transparency statement, and sub-processor list.
Draft internal records: processing register, impact assessment for high-risk processing, data-retention schedule, incident and breach procedure, and data-subject request procedure.
Set cross-border transfer mechanisms and document provider commitments on training use and retention.
Prepare a reusable answer bank for customer security and privacy questionnaires.
Schedule a review each quarter and on any change of model provider, data source, or agent capability.
deliverables: Privacy notice, AI transparency statement, sub-processor list
gates: Publication of any public policy
Classification of the AI use case
Any notification to a regulator or to customers
handoffs: `ops-security-and-reliability` for access, logging, and backup evidence

skills.name: legal-hiring-and-contractors
skills.title: Employment, Contractors, and Advisors
skills.purpose: Engage contractors, employees, and advisors correctly in each person's country, with IP and confidentiality secured and misclassification risk controlled.
inputs: Role, country of the worker, expected hours and duration, compensation
Whether the company has an entity in that country
workflow: Determine the engagement model allowed for the facts: contractor, employee through the company's entity, or employer-of-record. Apply the local tests for employee status and state the misclassification risk.
Research mandatory local terms: notice, probation, leave, social contributions, working time, and termination rules.
Draft the agreement with IP assignment, confidentiality, data protection, AI-tool usage rules, and post-termination restrictions that are enforceable locally.
Draft the offer letter and equity grant summary where relevant.
Produce the onboarding compliance checklist: right-to-work checks, registrations, payroll setup, policies to acknowledge.
Produce the offboarding checklist: access removal, IP and asset return, final pay, equity treatment.
gates: Engagement model for each person
Compensation and equity terms
Sending any offer or agreement

skills.name: legal-compliance-calendar
skills.title: Compliance Calendar and Corporate Housekeeping
skills.purpose: Maintain one calendar of every recurring obligation the company has, with owners, lead times, and evidence, so nothing lapses while the founder is building.
inputs: Entity type and jurisdiction, registration dates, financial year-end
Licences, registrations, trademarks, domains, insurance policies
Outputs of the other legal and finance skills
workflow: List obligations by source: company law (annual return, accounts, meetings), tax (returns, payments, registrations), employment, privacy and AI regulation, licences, IP renewals, insurance, and contractual commitments.
For each, record the rule source, due date or recurrence, lead time, preparer, approver, and where the evidence is filed.
Create the entries in ~~calendar with reminders at the lead time.
Run a monthly sweep: what is due in the next 60 days, what is overdue, what changed in the law or the business.
Run a quarterly health check: registers current, minute book complete, contracts register current, policies reviewed, trademark and domain status.
Report exceptions to the founder with the consequence of missing each one.
gates: Creation of calendar entries in the founder's calendar
Any filing or payment arising from the calendar

skills.name: legal-ip-and-trademarks
skills.title: Intellectual Property and Trademarks
skills.purpose: Protect what the company owns and avoid infringing what it does not: brand, code, data, models, and the open-source and third-party components the product is built on.
inputs: Brand names and logos, target markets
Codebase dependencies, datasets, model providers and their terms
workflow: Inventory IP assets: brand, domains, code, prompts, evaluation sets, datasets, fine-tuned weights, documentation, and trade secrets.
Run a preliminary trademark screen in the priority markets and classes; recommend filing strategy and order of countries; leave formal clearance and filing to a trademark attorney.
Audit open-source licences across dependencies; flag copyleft or non-commercial terms and model or dataset licences that restrict commercial use.
Review rights in training and retrieval data: source, licence, consent, and customer restrictions.
Summarize ownership of inputs and outputs under each model provider's terms and reflect it in customer contracts.
Assess patentability and the value of filing versus trade-secret protection; note disclosure deadlines.
Set trade-secret hygiene: access control, confidentiality terms, marking, and offboarding.
Record renewals and deadlines in the compliance calendar.
deliverables: Trademark screening memo and filing plan
gates: Any trademark or patent filing and its cost
Accepting a dependency or dataset with restrictive terms

skills.name: finance-setup
skills.title: Finance Stack Setup
skills.purpose: Stand up the finance foundation in the first days of the company: banking, payments, accounting system, chart of accounts, tax registrations, and the policies that make the monthly cycle run with minimal founder time.
inputs: Entity type, jurisdiction, financial year-end, functional currency
Revenue model (subscription, usage, services) and customer countries
Expected monthly transaction volume
workflow: Read `references/country-finance-checklist.md` and research the local requirements: accounting framework, bookkeeping and invoicing rules, e-invoicing mandates, record-retention period, and audit thresholds.
Recommend the bank or payment institution, payment processor, accounting system, and expense tool that work in the jurisdiction. Explain the choice in one paragraph each.

Design the chart of accounts on the local statutory layout, with dimensions useful to an AI company: model inference and cloud as cost of revenue, R&D, sales and marketing, general and administrative.
List required tax registrations (corporate income tax, VAT or GST or sales tax, payroll) with thresholds and deadlines.
Define accounting policies: revenue recognition for the pricing model, capitalisation of development costs if permitted, foreign-currency treatment, expense policy.
Configure the accounting system: bank feeds, tax codes, invoice template with mandatory local fields, document storage.
Set the finance calendar: weekly bookkeeping, monthly close, tax periods, year-end.
deliverables: Chart of accounts ready to import
gates: Choice of bank, processor, and accounting system
Any tax registration submission
Accounting policies

skills.name: finance-bookkeeping-and-close
skills.title: Bookkeeping and Month-End Close
skills.purpose: Run the record-to-report cycle: capture and code every transaction, reconcile, post accruals, and produce management accounts within five working days of month-end.
inputs: Bank, card, and payment-processor feeds or exports
Sales invoices, supplier bills, receipts, payroll reports
Prior-period trial balance
workflow: Weekly: pull transactions from ~~accounting system or exports, match each to a document, code to account and tax code, and list items that need the founder's answer.
Reconcile every bank, card, and processor account to statement balance. Explain every reconciling item.
Reconcile processor payouts to gross sales, fees, refunds, and chargebacks.
Post month-end entries: accruals, prepayments, depreciation, deferred revenue release, payroll, foreign-exchange revaluation, and usage-based costs from model and cloud providers.
Review the trial balance: variance to prior month and to budget, with an explanation for every movement above the materiality set in the profile.
Produce the management pack: profit and loss, balance sheet, cash flow, cash runway, and key metrics.
Lock the period and archive supporting documents under the local retention rules.
Keep a close checklist with sign-off per step and a list of open questions for the accountant.
deliverables: Monthly management pack and variance commentary
gates: Posting of manual journals
Any transaction the documents do not explain
Period lock
handoffs: `finance-tax-and-statutory-compliance` for returns built on the ledger

skills.name: finance-invoicing-and-collections
skills.title: Invoicing, Revenue, and Collections
skills.purpose: Operate order-to-cash: turn closed deals into compliant invoices or subscriptions, recognise revenue correctly, collect on time, and report recurring revenue.
inputs: Signed order or checkout record, price, term, billing frequency, customer tax details
Usage data for metered pricing
Receivables ageing
workflow: Create the customer and the contract record with billing terms, tax treatment by customer location, and purchase-order or portal requirements.
Issue invoices that meet local mandatory content and any e-invoicing channel; for self-serve, configure plans, metering, proration, and dunning in ~~payments.
Determine indirect tax per sale (place of supply, reverse charge, marketplace or digital-services rules, exemption certificates).
Build the revenue schedule: performance obligations, deferred revenue, usage true-ups.
Run collections weekly: ageing review, reminder sequence at set intervals, escalation, and dispute log. Draft each reminder for approval.
Process refunds, credit notes, and chargebacks with an audit trail.
Report monthly: recurring revenue movements (new, expansion, contraction, churn), days sales outstanding, and cash collected.
deliverables: Invoices, credit notes, and billing configuration
gates: Sending invoices and reminders until the founder approves a standing rule
Credit notes, refunds, write-offs
Tax treatment of a new country or product

skills.name: finance-payables-and-payroll
skills.title: Payables, Expenses, and Payroll
skills.purpose: Operate procure-to-pay and payroll: capture bills, verify them, schedule payments against cash, pay people correctly, and keep vendor and tool spend under control.
inputs: Supplier bills, subscriptions, contractor invoices, receipts
Payroll data: people, pay, benefits, country
Cash balance and forecast
workflow: Capture bills from the inbox or uploads; extract vendor, amount, tax, due date, and service period; detect duplicates.
Verify each bill against the contract or order and code it to account, cost centre, and tax code.
Maintain the vendor register: tax details, payment terms, contract renewal dates, and withholding obligations for foreign vendors.
Propose a weekly payment run ranked by due date and criticality against available cash. Stage payments; never release them.
Track recurring SaaS, model-API, and cloud spend; flag unused seats, price changes, and committed-spend opportunities.
Prepare payroll per country: gross-to-net, employer contributions, filings, and payslips through the local payroll provider or employer-of-record.
Prepare contractor payments with required invoices and year-end reporting forms.
Process founder expenses and reimbursements under the expense policy.
deliverables: Coded bills and proposed payment run
Payroll preparation file and filing checklist
Monthly spend report with savings actions
gates: Release of every payment run and payroll
New vendor bank details or changes to them
Cancelling or committing to any subscription

skills.name: finance-tax-and-statutory-compliance
skills.title: Tax and Statutory Compliance
skills.purpose: Prepare every tax return and statutory report the company's legal form and country require, on time, with a file a local accountant can review and submit quickly.
inputs: Closed ledger for the period
Registrations held and filing frequencies
Cross-border sales, purchases, staff, and related-party transactions
workflow: Build the obligations list for the entity and jurisdiction: corporate income tax, indirect tax, payroll taxes, withholding, statutory accounts, annual return, and any startup-specific regime.
For each indirect-tax period, reconcile the return to the ledger, apply cross-border rules, and prepare the return workpaper.
Estimate corporate tax quarterly and at year-end, including loss carry-forwards and instalments.
Identify incentives the company may qualify for (R&D credits, innovation or startup status, grants) and assemble the technical and cost evidence as work happens.
Assess cross-border exposure: taxable presence created by remote staff or agents, transfer pricing between group entities, and digital-services rules.
Prepare year-end: cut-off, accrual review, fixed assets, equity movements, notes, and the statutory-format accounts in the local framework.
Assemble the accountant pack: trial balance, reconciliations, workpapers, and open questions.
Record filing confirmations and payments in the compliance calendar.
deliverables: Year-end accounts pack in statutory format
Incentive eligibility memo and evidence file
gates: Every submission to a tax authority or registry
Every tax payment
Positions involving judgment (incentive claims, cross-border treatment)

skills.name: finance-planning-and-runway
skills.title: Financial Model, Budget, and Runway
skills.purpose: Give the founder a current view of cash, runway, and unit economics, with a model that reflects how AI companies actually earn and spend: usage-driven revenue and inference-driven cost of revenue.
inputs: Actuals from the ledger, pipeline from the CRM, pricing and packaging
Token, model, and cloud cost per unit of product usage
Hiring and spend plans
workflow: Build a driver-based model: leads to customers through funnel conversion, price and usage per customer, churn and expansion.
Model cost of revenue per unit of work: tokens per task, model mix, caching and batch discounts, retries, human-in-the-loop time, cloud, and support.
Compute unit economics: gross margin per customer and per task, acquisition cost, payback, lifetime value, and sensitivity to model price changes.
Build the 13-week cash forecast and the 24-month plan with base, downside, and upside cases.
State runway in months and the date cash reaches the founder's minimum buffer. List the three levers with the largest effect.
Set the budget and compare actuals monthly, explaining variances.
Produce the monthly investor or board update: metrics, cash, wins, problems, asks.
deliverables: Financial model workbook with assumptions tab
gates: Core assumptions (pricing, conversion, churn, cost per task)
Anything sent to investors or the board

skills.name: finance-fundraising-and-investor-relations
skills.title: Fundraising Process and Investor Relations
skills.purpose: Run the raise as a managed pipeline and keep investors informed afterwards: narrative, deck, target list, outreach, meetings, diligence, and regular updates. The legal mechanics sit in `legal-fundraising`.
inputs: Traction, metrics, financial model, amount and use of funds
Founder's network and target investor geography
workflow: Decide whether and when to raise from runway, milestones, and alternatives (revenue, grants, non-dilutive programs available in the HQ country).
Write the narrative: problem, insight, product, proof, market, business model, why this founder, and what the money achieves.
Build the deck and a short memo; one message per slide; every number sourced from the model.
Build the investor list by stage, sector, geography, and cheque size; find the warmest path to each.
Run the process in a pipeline with stages, next steps, and dates; batch meetings to create momentum.
Prepare for each meeting: investor background, likely questions, and honest answers to the hard ones.
Manage diligence requests from the data room and track open items.
After closing, send a monthly update: metrics, cash, wins, problems, asks.
deliverables: Investor update template and monthly updates
gates: Amount, valuation expectations, and timing
Any material sent to investors
Metrics and forward-looking statements shared externally
handoffs: `legal-fundraising` for instruments, term sheets, and closing

skills.name: marketing-positioning-and-messaging
skills.title: Positioning, Messaging, and Product Marketing
skills.purpose: Define who the product is for, what job it does, why it wins, and how to say it, then turn that into the messaging source every other marketing and sales skill draws on.
inputs: Product description, evidence from customer conversations, competitors and alternatives
Target segment hypotheses
workflow: Define the ideal customer profile and buying committee: firmographics, trigger events, pains in the customer's words, and current alternative (including doing nothing or hiring people).
Research the competitive set, including incumbent software, other AI entrants, and in-house builds on foundation models.
Write the positioning statement: category, target, problem, outcome delivered, proof, and differentiator. For agentic products, state the unit of work the agent completes and the outcome sold.
Build the messaging hierarchy: one-line promise, three pillars each with proof points, objection responses, and the trust message (accuracy, oversight, data handling).
Write persona-specific versions for economic buyer, user, and technical evaluator.
Produce launch assets list and the product-marketing plan for each release: audience, message, channels, enablement.
Create competitive battlecards with honest strengths and weaknesses.
Define how the messaging will be tested (landing-page variants, outbound reply rates, sales-call reactions) and when it is revisited.
gates: Target segment choice
Final positioning and any comparative claim about a competitor

skills.name: marketing-brand-and-design
skills.title: Brand Identity and Design System
skills.purpose: Give the company a coherent identity and a reusable design system so a single founder can produce consistent website, product, deck, and social assets quickly.
inputs: Positioning and audience
Names, visual references, or existing assets the founder likes or rejects
workflow: Generate name candidates and screen each for domain availability, obvious trademark conflicts in the target markets, and meaning in the main customer languages. Leave formal clearance to a trademark professional.
Define brand foundations: purpose, personality, voice and tone rules with do and don't examples.
Define the visual system: logo direction, color palette with accessibility contrast checked, typography, spacing, iconography, and illustration or imagery style.
Express the system as design tokens that both the website and the product UI consume.
Produce core templates: pitch deck, one-pager, social post formats, email signature, document template.
Write the brand guidelines as a short reference a contractor could follow.
Build assets in ~~design tool where connected; otherwise deliver specifications and editable files.
gates: Company and product name
Logo and palette
Purchase of domains or trademark applications
handoffs: `legal-commercial-contracts` or a trademark professional for filings

skills.name: marketing-website
skills.title: Website and Landing Pages
skills.purpose: Ship a website that explains the product, earns trust, and converts visitors into trials, demos, or waitlist sign-ups, with analytics in place from the first visit.
inputs: Messaging hierarchy, brand system, pricing, proof (demos, results, logos, security posture)
Conversion goal: self-serve sign-up, demo request, or waitlist

Build dashboards: system health, AI quality and cost, business activity.
Configure alerts on objective burn and hard failures, routed to the founder's phone with a link to the runbook; remove alerts that never lead to action.
Add external uptime checks and a public status page.
Review weekly: incidents, slow paths, error classes, cost anomalies.
gates: Storing prompt or response content
Alert routing and quiet hours

skills.name: ops-incident-response
skills.title: Incident Response
skills.purpose: Restore service fast, tell customers the truth, and learn from each incident, including incidents where the AI acted wrongly.
inputs: Alert or report, dashboards, logs, recent changes
workflow: Declare the incident, set severity, and start a timeline.
Stabilize first: roll back the last change, disable the affected feature or agent action, or fail over. Diagnose after impact stops.
For AI incidents, stop the behavior with the kill switch or by reducing autonomy, then identify affected customers and actions taken.
Investigate with evidence: what changed, what the metrics and traces show, which hypothesis each fact supports.
Communicate at set intervals: status page, affected customers, and internal log. Draft each message for approval.
Verify recovery against the service indicators and close the incident.
Assess notification duties (customers, regulators, insurers) with the legal skills when data or regulated activity is involved.
Write a blameless review: timeline, impact, root causes, what worked, and corrective actions with owners and dates.
Update runbooks, alerts, tests, and evaluations from the review.
gates: Customer and public communications
Destructive remediation steps
Regulatory notifications

skills.name: ops-cost-and-finops
skills.title: Cloud and AI Cost Management
skills.purpose: Keep the cost of running the product visible per customer and per task, and lower it without lowering quality.
inputs: Cloud and model-provider billing, usage traces, pricing and margin targets
workflow: Tag and attribute spend by environment, service, customer, and task type.
Compute cost per successful task and gross margin per customer; rank the outliers.
Set budgets and alerts per provider and hard limits per tenant.
Reduce model cost in order of safety: remove waste (retries, oversized context), cache, batch non-urgent work, route simple steps to smaller models, then renegotiate or commit.
Verify each change against the evaluation suite before and after.
Right-size infrastructure, remove idle resources, and use commitments only for stable baseline load.
Forecast spend against growth and feed the financial model.
Report monthly: spend, unit cost trend, savings made, next actions.
gates: Committed-spend contracts
Changes that trade quality for cost
Deleting resources

skills.name: ops-security-and-reliability
skills.title: Infrastructure Security, Reliability, and Compliance Readiness
skills.purpose: Run infrastructure to the standard enterprise customers audit against, sized for a one-person company, with evidence collected as work happens.
inputs: Infrastructure, customer security requirements, target frameworks
workflow: Set the control baseline: single sign-on and multi-factor everywhere, least-privilege roles, no shared accounts, device security, logging of administrative actions.
Manage secrets and keys: storage, rotation, and removal on offboarding.
Manage vulnerabilities: patching cadence, dependency and image scanning, external scan or penetration test before enterprise sales.
Define reliability targets: recovery time and recovery point; implement backups, redundancy, and a tested disaster-recovery procedure.
Write the minimum policy set that matches actual practice: access, change, incident, vendor, data handling, business continuity.
Map controls to the target framework and identify gaps; automate evidence collection.
Maintain the vendor and sub-processor inventory with security review notes.
Publish a trust page: practices, sub-processors, certifications in progress, contact.
gates: Engaging auditors or testers
Access changes for production
Published security claims

skills.name: support-setup
skills.title: Support Operations Setup
skills.purpose: Design a support operation one founder can sustain: clear channels, published commitments, automation for the routine, and a fast path to the founder for what matters.
inputs: Customer segments and plans, product complexity, time zones, tools in the profile
workflow: Choose channels by segment: in-product chat, email, shared channel for enterprise, community forum; avoid channels that cannot be staffed.
Set service commitments per plan: hours, first-response and resolution targets, severity definitions.
Configure ~~helpdesk: inbox, forms that collect the needed details, tags, priorities, routing, and customer context from the CRM and product.
Define the ticket lifecycle and escalation path, including engineering bugs and security or privacy reports.
Write saved replies for the common cases in the brand voice.
Define support metrics: volume by category, response and resolution times, deflection rate, satisfaction, and contact rate per active customer.
Publish the support policy and how to reach support.
gates: Published service commitments
Helpdesk vendor and paid plan

skills.name: support-ai-agent
skills.title: AI Support Agent
skills.purpose: Resolve routine customer questions instantly and correctly with an AI agent, and hand everything else to the founder with full context.
inputs: Knowledge base, product documentation, past tickets, support policy
Systems the agent may read or act on
workflow: Select the ticket categories suitable for automation by volume, risk, and availability of a documented answer.
Define agent scope: what it answers, what it may do (look up status, reset, refund within limits), and what it must never do.
Ground the agent in the knowledge base and account data; require an answer to be supported by a source or else hand off.
Write hand-off rules: frustration, repeated contact, billing disputes, legal or security topics, low confidence, or customer request for a person.
Make the hand-off complete: summary, steps tried, account context, suggested reply.
Disclose that the customer is talking to an AI where required or expected.
Evaluate before launch on past tickets; set accuracy and escalation thresholds.
Review weekly: resolved without human, wrong answers, hand-off reasons; fix the knowledge gap or the prompt.
gates: Actions the agent may take on accounts or money
Launch to customers
handoffs: `support-setup` for channels, commitments, and escalation paths

skills.name: support-ticket-triage-and-response
skills.title: Ticket Triage and Response
skills.purpose: Classify every incoming request, answer what can be answered, and escalate the rest with everything the next person needs.
inputs: Ticket queue, customer and account context, knowledge base, known issues
workflow: Read the queue; classify each ticket by category, severity, customer tier, and sentiment; detect duplicates and incident clusters.
Order work by service commitment and severity.
Research each ticket: account history, product logs, known issues, documentation.
Draft the reply: answer first, clear steps, honest status when there is no fix yet, and the next update time.
For bugs, reproduce where possible and write the engineering report: steps, expected and actual, evidence, impact.
For feature requests, log with customer and context to the feedback store.
For billing, legal, security, or privacy matters, route to the matching skill and tell the customer what happens next.
Close with confirmation; tag the root cause; record whether documentation would have prevented the ticket.
gates: Sending replies until a standing rule is approved per category
Refunds, credits, and exceptions
Any admission of fault or liability

skills.name: support-knowledge-base
skills.title: Knowledge Base and Documentation
skills.purpose: Maintain documentation that answers customers' questions before they ask, and that the support agent and AI answer engines can rely on.
inputs: Product, release notes, ticket categories, search queries with no result
workflow: Structure the knowledge base: getting started, how-to guides by task, reference, troubleshooting, account and billing, security and data.
Prioritize articles by ticket volume and onboarding drop-off.
Write each article for one task: outcome, prerequisites, numbered steps, expected result, common errors.
Explain AI behavior plainly: what the product can and cannot do, how to review its work, how data is used.
Document the API and integrations with working examples.
Review every article against the product before publishing and on every release that touches it.
Publish through ~~knowledge base and make the content available to the support agent.
Measure: views, helpfulness ratings, searches without results, tickets per article topic.
deliverables: Content gap list and review schedule
gates: Publishing articles
Statements about data handling or guarantees

skills.name: support-customer-success
skills.title: Customer Onboarding, Success, and Retention
skills.purpose: Get each customer to the outcome they bought, keep them, and grow the account, using health signals and automation in place of a success team.
inputs: Closed-won hand-over brief, usage and quality data, support history, contract dates
workflow: Define the onboarding path per segment: milestones to first value, owner of each step, target days.
Run onboarding: kickoff, setup and integration, first successful task, training, hand-over to steady state; automate reminders and checks.
Define the health score: usage, task success, breadth of adoption, support load, sentiment, payment behavior, champion status.
Review health weekly; act on declines with a specific play.
Run lifecycle communications: tips, new capabilities, results achieved.
Prepare business reviews that show outcomes in the customer's terms.
Manage renewals from 90 days out; identify expansion from usage and unmet needs.
Collect satisfaction and reference willingness; ask satisfied customers for reviews, referrals, and case studies.
On churn, interview and record the cause.
deliverables: Health score definition and weekly risk list
gates: Customer communications until a standing rule is approved
Commercial offers for renewals or saves
